rounds.fact: ESPN.com launched in 1995 and quickly became one of the most-visited sites on the early web, built around a dense grid of scores and headlines that's still recognizable in sports sites today.
Microsoft's homepage in the late 90s was essentially a portal to its own products, years before it settled into the cleaner corporate design language it uses today.
Allrecipes built its entire catalog from user-submitted recipes rather than professional chefs, an early example of crowdsourced content outperforming edited, expert-driven sites.
Digg pioneered the user-voted news-aggregation format years before Reddit took over that space, and a single controversial 2010 redesign is often cited as the reason it lost most of its audience.
Palm's PDAs were the dominant handheld computers of the late 90s, and its site sold both the devices and a marketplace of tiny downloadable apps years before smartphones existed.
